content: 1. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir is indicated for the treatment of hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotypes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 in patients who have previously been treated with an NS5A inhibitor-containing regimen. It is also indicated for genotypes 1a or 3 in patients previously treated with a sofosbuvir-containing regimen without an NS5A inhibitor. The recommended dosage is one tablet (sofosbuvir 400 mg/velpatasvir 100 mg/voxilaprevir 100 mg) taken orally once daily for 12 weeks. 2. All patients should be tested for evidence of current or prior hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection by measuring hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc) before initiating treatment, as per the Black Box Warnings. 3. The safety and efficacy of this regimen have not been established in certain populations or conditions. 4. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of alpelisib by inhibiting certain transporters. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If unavoidable, monitor closely for increased adverse reactions. 7. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If unavoidable, evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect. 8. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 9. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 10. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 11. Ceftobiprole medocaril sodium increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting OATP1B1/1B3 transporters. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 12. Velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of colchicine by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If unavoidable, reduce the colchicine dose or frequency as per prescribing information. Co-administration is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 13. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 14. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 15. Darolutamide increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions and consider dose reduction of the BCRP substrate drug. 16. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 17. Enasidenib increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inhibiting OATP1B1, OATP1B3, and BCRP transporters. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If unavoidable, reduce the substrate dosage as per prescribing information. 18. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 19. Fexinidazole decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism and increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 20. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 21. Fostemsavir increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 and BCRP transporters. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative HCV regimen should be used. 22. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 23. Givosiran increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 24. Lasmiditan increases the levels of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inhibiting BCRP and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 25. Leniolisib increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inhibiting BCRP, OATP1B1, and OATP1B3 transporters. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 26. Lonafarnib increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 27. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 28. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 29. Mitotane decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 30. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 31. Velpatasvir increases the toxicity of ozanimod by inhibiting BCRP transporters, leading to increased exposure of ozanimod metabolites. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 32. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 33. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 34. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 35. Voxilaprevir increases the levels or effects of resmetirom by inhibiting certain transporters. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 36. Velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of revefenacin by inhibiting OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters. Co-administration is not recommended. 37. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 38. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 39. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 40. Velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 41. Sotorasib decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 42. Voxilaprevir increases the levels or effects of sulbactam/durlobactam by inhibiting OATP1 transporters. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 43. Velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of talazoparib by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 44. Tepotinib increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 45. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 46. Trofinetide increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 47. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used.
